And I think you're referring -- in fact, it's clear that you're referring to -- under paragraph 1 where it says "order," it's about the third paragraph down, where it says: "Establish full cooperation with the organs of government in Sanski Most Municipality and collaboration with TO and police units." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you agree with me that if this had just been normal peacetime conditions, let's say we're in 1985, and the JNA had decided to establish a military base in the Sanski Most area and had sent a military unit there, would you agree with me that there would have been an order saying "establish full cooperation with the organs of government in the Sanski Most Municipality and collaboration with TO and police units"? In other words, what I'm suggesting is that is common language any time a unit moves into a new civilian area. Peacetime, wartime, any time.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I can't really tell you what would be expected and the type of regulations that would be passed out in 1985 or in a period of peacetime. I can tell you this was more emphatic because it was a period of some tension and crisis. That unit had been involved in combat operations since late 1991 and it was moving back into an area that -- or moving back into the Krajina, which clearly had tensions. So I can only go by what this particular instruction says. I don't know if in 1985 it would have been less emphatic or it would have been covered in some standard operating procedure that would have had been written. So I'm not clear. I'm not sure I can really answer the question fully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think in your experience, you certainly have become aware that military orders tend to be written in the same language over and over and over to cover the same situation. So I take it it wouldn't surprise you to find an order from 1985 where a unit was moving into a community where it had not been to find this language in that order. It wouldn't surprise you, would it?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: In this case, this is not a unit that is necessarily moving back into an area that it has never been before. It is moving back into an area that it had been based in. So I'm not sure if it would surprise me or not to be honest. If you said to me here's an instruction from 1985 that has very little reference to establishing coordination with the police and civilian authorities and made reference to some generic standing operation procedure, would that surprise me? No. Would it surprise me in 1985 if there was an instruction which was more emphatic and echoed some of this language? Maybe not. So I'm not sure I can really answer the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm having difficulty asking it in a way that probably makes sense to you. From my own military experience, I know that the presence of a military base, a military unit in a community has significant impact on that community. And that cooperation between the military and the civilian authorities is awfully important in dealing with all of the impacts that come from that. I think you can probably agree with that.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, clearly a military unit in a community, you know, has its own issues to deal with and cooperation between civilian bodies and the police and other structures is a feature of that relationship. So -- and that's not unusual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is 1 April 1992, the date of this document we're looking at. Do you know what the nature of the Sanski Most organs of government was at that time?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: No, I'm unclear on the nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that this was well before the Serb takeover of the Sanski Most organs of government and that it was a multiethnic government at that point?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the takeover was in late May, so I'm not sure it was well before the takeover. A matter of weeks. I know it was a multiethnic municipality, but I'm unclear on the details of the structure of government and how they operated in that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, does the significance of that paragraph that you've referred us to, about establishing full cooperation, change if it's establishing full cooperation with a multiparty government made up of primarily Serbs and Muslims, or if it's establishing cooperation with a purely Serb municipality? Do you think the significance is different as to which one it's dealing with?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, it could very well change that. But I'm a little bit unclear on the exact details or necessarily what that particular brigade actually did in reality in terms of its cooperation and who it cooperated with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a matter of record in this case that the Serbian Municipality of Sanski Most was not formed until 20 April. Okay? So clearly this is referring to a pre-Serbian Municipality of Sanski Most government, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, it would appear to be so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition, let me see if I can find it, maybe you know where it is, this order indicates that the mission of the brigade to prevent interethnic conflict, among other things.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's the paragraph above. That's what is stated in this instruction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Okay, I think I'm finished with that. We'll go now in your report to paragraph 1.112. In this paragraph of your report, you say this: In a similar manner to the municipal level, cooperative links were also established. And again, we're still in that section dealing with cooperation between military, civilian bodies. "Cooperative links were also established with the regional government bodies including the Autonomous Region of Krajina, ARK, Crisis Staff; the Autonomous Region of Krajina Assembly; and other regional governmental bodies. On 14 April 1992, a reference in a corps report noted that the 5th corps command focussed its work on informing subordinate units, organising a meeting between the SAO of Krajina commander and commanders of subordinate staffs in monitoring the situation in the area of responsibility." That's what you tell us. Right?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the documents you refer to in 173 I have now marked as DB268, and I'll ask you to take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, does this document that Mr. Ackerman is tendering now already have a number, according to your records? Has it been tendered by the Prosecution or is it a new?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd have to check that, Your Honour. Ms. Gustin tells me that it is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Gustin. Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: While I'm up, I wonder if we could have a very short break, about 5 minutes, and let the witness read the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you object to that, Mr. Ackerman? You were in the middle of a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We were going to have a break in 15 minutes, but if somebody needs a break for some reason, I have no objection at all., we'll do it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Let's break now. We'll have a break of 25 minutes straight away. I think we can have the break now and continue afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it fine with you, Mr. Ackerman? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, we were just getting ready to look at the Document DB268. And as I understand, this was not previously an exhibit in the case. First thing I'll draw to your attention is it's dated 14 April 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we just start reading it, looking at that first paragraph, it's talking about a fierce attack launched by the Ustashas from Pakrac, Lipik, Prekopakra, Klisa, and Matkovac areas. That's all in Croatia, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you go on down to the second paragraph, again talking about Croatia, Medarski, Vinograd, Nova Gradiska, Bilici village, all those villages are Croatian?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I think they are. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you go down to paragraph 2, the area and villages discussed there and the reference to Ustashas all have to do with the battle that was going on in Croatia, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this report, of course, was issued during a time when the -- I believe the 5th Corps command was located in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, just over the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The paragraph that you refer to in your paragraph 1.112, it's there close to the bottom: "The 5th Corps command focussed its work on informing subordinate units organising a meeting between the SAO Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina commander and commanders of subordinate staffs and monitoring the situation in the area of responsibility." Again, that's talking about the SAO Krajina, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it is, and I think the reference that I'm making more generally is made in this paragraph, that the corps was used to or had done in Western Slavonia, had contacts with regional government bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what you told the Chamber, referring to a document that was not an exhibit, so they couldn't check it, in a similar manner to the municipal level, cooperative links were also established with the regional government bodies --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I just want to say for the record obviously Mr. Brown has no control over what becomes an exhibit and what doesn't, and I don't like the suggestion that that was somehow -- that there was some intent to put in something without putting in the exhibit on Mr. Brown's part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Definitely not, Mr. Nicholls. But sooner or later, I think, and probably much sooner than later, rather than later, you will have to face this problem because you have got several reports referring to several documents that are not in the record as exhibits. What's the solution for that? It's not my business. It's your business. So you have a clear indication from Mr. Ackerman today that that is something that he attaches importance to. And if we found or we came across the word "justifiably" before, I think I can also use the word justifiably now because it's a problem. I mean, what's not in the record will remain outside the record. I mean, I'm not going to refer to those documents that are not tendered an exhibit even if I have them. You have filed binders with hundreds if not thousands of documents that have ultimately not been tendered in evidence. Perfectly legitimate. I agree that that could be done, but I think you need to address this problem and find a solution, or at least a solution that you are satisfied with. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, what you told the Chamber in paragraph 1.112 was this: "In a similar manner to the municipal level, cooperative links were also established -- were also established -- with the regional government bodies, including the Autonomous Region of Krajina, ARK, Crisis Staff; the Autonomous Region of Krajina Assembly; and other regional government bodies. On 14 April 1992, a reference in a corps report noted that." You are citing that as support for what you just said about these cooperative links being established with -- and the major one there is the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: It's not the only one there, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's just not correct, is it? That's totally misleading, isn't it? You're referring to a document from Croatia dealing with the SAO Krajina in Croatia as support for the proposition that cooperative links were established with the ARK Crisis Staff. I find that unacceptable, don't you?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Well, I think maybe if you read on to the next paragraph, Mr. Ackerman, you'll see that there are enough references there talking about more regional ARK Crisis Staffs, Autonomous Region of Krajina Assembly documents. My point in this whole paragraph, this whole section in relation to cooperation with civilian authorities, was that the corps established cooperative links with government bodies wherever it went. The SAO in Krajina, in Western Slavonia, was a regional body that they established some contact with as can be seen from this document, amongst others, I hasten to say, because I think I talk about that in Western Slavonia paragraph. This chapter is about cooperation with civilian authorities. Now, in paragraph 1.113, I list and footnote other references that talk about more specifically the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going there, but I'm talking about 1.112 right now. You're talking about April of 1992. There wasn't even an ARK Crisis Staff at that point, was there?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: No, I don't believe there was. But I'm not making there was a claim there was an ARK Crisis Staff in that reference. In paragraph 1.112 I make reference that, as well as at municipal level, there were established links with other regional government bodies. This was one of them, the one in Croatia. There were also ones in the Krajina of which I come on to in 1.113.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's go to point 1.113. In 1.113, you tell us this, and I'll leave out a little bit just to provide context: "General Major Talic assisted ARK personnel in the execution of their tasks." Do you see that? Do you see that language in your report, 1.113?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the conclusion that would be logically drawn from that, I think, is that several ARK personnel were assisted by General Talic in the execution of several tasks because it's all plural "personnel and tasks." Right?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to look at the Document DB269. This is the document you refer the Chamber to to support that proposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And again, Your Honours, I don't think this was a document that was previously admitted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the document?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I do, yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you tendering it yourself, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I am. I'm tendering as DB269.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a permit, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's a permit issued to -- just, it's easy to just read the whole thing: "This document is to certify that permission has been granted for a delegation to travel along the Doboj/Prnjavor route. The delegation from the Serbian Republic of BH and Banja Luka is headed by Mr. Radoslav Brdjanin. The delegation has another nine people with four motor vehicles. This permit cannot be used for other purposes." Now, you say this proves that ARK personnel were assisted. What other personnel are there in there other than Mr. Brdjanin that are ARK personnel?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Brdjanin clearly is a member of the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff. It doesn't make mention that they were -- specifically who exactly the other nine personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you used the word "personnel" that's plural. Who else in that report is ARK personnel?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: In that particular one, there's not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that's the one you cited?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: But there are other references in that paragraph that talk about --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's only one other reference to that phrase, "assisted ARK personnel in the execution of their tasks." You cite -- you cite footnote 178 and this is the document.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I could also have cited document footnote number 187, which is the visit to Manjaca camp, which is in an assistance issue --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to get to that. We're going to talk about that. Let me focus you on the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Ackerman, before you proceed, may I ask you, please, to have a look at your DB269A and your DB269B. I hope you're not suggesting that DB269A is a faithful translation of DB269B. Because although it should be, there's no way it could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I hope it is, Your Honour. It's possible that got confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's definitely -- there's a confusion here. Everyone makes mistakes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well I'm looking at it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's probably -- but we need to know because if you're going to make use of the English translation of what we have as 269B, you need to dig that up. And we don't really need us, the three Judges at least, the translation into B/C/S of what is purported to be 269A. Because I don't think we need it. But perhaps you could help us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, there's clearly a problem, Your Honour. The one here on my computer is the correct one. The one has been given to you is not. It's some other document completely

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The one that has been given to us has the ERN number 00861601.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's clearly the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I'm just drawing your attention to this, and then you see to it later. I don't want to take up -- of your cross-examination time, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'll definitely substitute the proper document. I have it right here. Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, we're back to this document, this permit. Is there anything in that that indicates what was going on here was a task of ARK?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Well, all I can say is that Mr. Brdjanin was not a member who is been given assistance in being able to travel in this area on the 26th of June 1992, two days after operation corridor was launched by the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I really want to insist that you answer my question. Is there anything in this document that indicates that was going on here was a task of ARK? That's the question I asked you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Directly stated in this document, it doesn't say this was a task of the ARK. What it does say is that Mr. Brdjanin is heading a delegation into this area, and he is request -- or he has been granted permission by General Talic for him and other people to go into this area which at that time was a combat zone, and also you remember my direct testimony in the video reference Mr. Brdjanin makes about visiting the corridor area. It does not say specifically this was a task of the ARK.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a conclusion that you came to having read or perused other material.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But Mr. Ackerman is also correct in his suggestion that that does not follow from the document itself, from the face of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It doesn't state that specifically, that it was an ARK task, but you have a very influential --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we are there. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My only point, Your Honour, was that I believe the witness was trying to answer the question. As he did, Mr. Ackerman keeps cutting him off midsentence, and I object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, yes, Mr. Ackerman. Please don't cut the witness mid -- okay, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if I ask about an orange and he starts talking about an apple, can I ask him to focus on the orange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but please be patient. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would just like to add as well that the reference actually says,"assisted ARK personnel in the execution of their tasks." It doesn't actually say the execution of ARK tasks. But my reference is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But we are now, you know, getting lost in useless meanders. Let's proceed. Mr. Ackerman, next question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have no idea what this delegation was about, do you? You'd have no idea what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: On the basis of this document, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, this is the concern: You told the Chamber that General Talic assisted ARK personnel in the execution of their tasks. Now, the Chamber would have been entitled to believe that that's exactly the case, that General Talic assisted ARK personnel, multiple people, in the execution of their tasks, multiple tasks, and you cite a document that's not an exhibit in the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop telling him that because I agree with the submission of Mr. Nicholls --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So do I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- That's not a fault that could be attributed to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Please, I'm not attributing it to him. What I'm trying to suggest that it is unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's argument, not a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are correct. Just put a question, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm finished with the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we'll move to the next.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the same paragraph, you talk about the ARK Crisis Staff and its relation to or impact on military matters. 2 t reads like this: Conversely, decisions or discussion at the ARK Crisis Staff meetings and other regional level bodies impacted on or were related to military activity. These included, for example," and then you go through a list of things. And one of those is: "And issues in relation to camps." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would it be -- would it be appropriate for someone reading that to draw the conclusion that issues in relation to camps were discussed at ARK Crisis Staff meetings, that that's what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Not -- no. I'm saying that the issue of camps were discussed at certain meetings, and I reference one of them which is a report which made mention of the autonomous region Crisis Staff, or the autonomous region war presidency meeting discussing the issue of camps as footnote 184. And there's other references in the paragraph talking about visits to camps by delegates. So no, I'm not implying that it's ARK Crisis Staff meetings that necessarily -- that -- in your question that they were discussing camps all the time, but there are references that I've seen which discuss the issue of camps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe you misunderstood my question, and it's probably my fault. If you read the whole thing, starting with "conversely" down to the word "camps," would it be inappropriate for someone to conclude that you're suggesting that the ARK Crisis Staff in a meeting discussed issues in relation to camps? Would that be a mistake if someone were to conclude that?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I'm a little unclear on the question. Maybe it's me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, it's not you. It's actually the first of this series of -- sequence of sentences in your report because basically you have the interchanging -- interchangeable use of decisions or discussions. Then ARK Crisis Staff meetings and other regional level bodies. And then whether they impacted on or were merely related to military activity. And then a series of topics, and it's not quite clear whether it's decisions and discussions or decisions, or mere discussions, or just the issue. I mean, if you read it, these included, for example, decisions and discussions on mobilisation, deadlines concerning the surrender of weapons, the removal of non-Serbs from the military, decisions relating to the establishment of civilian authorities and issues in relation to camp. What are we talking about now, decisions on issues in relation to camps or just discussions on issues relating to camps? I mean, I fully understand the legitimacy of Mr. Ackerman's question and his concern, too, because I mean things need to be clear. What is one to understand in reading through this part of the paragraph with regard to camps, only? Forget the rest, because the question does not address the others, the other topics.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With regard to camps, in the footnote I cited, it was a discussion I believe to do with the International Red Cross and whether the Red Cross were being fair, I think, in relation to their --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that's one issue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is one issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Here you say "issues."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe I have made an error in putting it like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's okay. No one is blaming you for that. We just want a clear-cut answer as to what am I supposed to understand when I'm reading this. Because here, I have a reference to a document which irrespective of whether it's in the records or not, that's not your problem, that's the Prosecution's problem. But even reading this, what conclusion am I supposed to come to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think in this particular reference, that the issue of camps was known about. It was reported as a result of a war presidency meeting that the assistant commander for civilian affairs of the 1st Krajina Corps had visited, and he was passing on that comment and discussion about the issue of camps at that time. My point, and maybe I should have articulated the paragraph in a better way, was that there were discussions. This was not a report about the functioning and the inner workings of these government bodies. What I wanted to articulate was that there were discussions and decisions, and maybe I should have made it more clear in relation to which was a decision and which was a discussion. About military or Defence-related issues at this level that this was not a body or these bodies including the ARK Crisis Staff were not bodies that were divorced completely from discussing and taking decisions related to military issues. Some of those of some significance, like weapon deadlines, like the removal of non-Serbs from the military, and others were more discussions about awareness of certain issues -- involved, for example, the issue of camps. Apologise if I've made the paragraph unclear. This was not a paragraph or a part of the report that was going into all the workings and all the decisions of this -- these regional and other government bodies. That is not within the remit of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's -- okay, I thank you for that. But you also need to understand that this is something that is fundamentally important, at least for part of this trial, because there is an allegation on the part of the Prosecution that what was happening in the camps was known, was known to all -- to everyone, and still the ARK Crisis Staff, for example, deliberately chose to not to discuss this matter or try to avoid discussing this matter. So you can understand why Mr. Ackerman is concerned about this matter, which should also be of concern to the Prosecution. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you say in the paragraph was that -- you used the words "impacted on or related to military activity." And then go on to cite issues in relation to the camps. And the document you cite there is DB270, and I'd like you to look at that now, please. And please feel free to look at the entire document, but specifically I think you were referring to page 2, paragraph 3: "humanitarian organisations are operating in these areas. We still have certain complaints about the work of the NCK, International Red Cross Committee, because they keeps their methods of work and information about the conditions found in the camps to themselves and probably for their superiors. At one of the AR war presidency meetings, they were warned, but their response was that they were not obliged to inform anyone of the conditions they find in camps except their authorised institutions." Now is that the paragraph you were referring to when you suggested that the ARK Crisis Staff had, in their meetings, taken decisions or had discussions that impacted on or related to military activity?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, in relation to the camps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, first of all, isn't it a bit of a stretch to say that what's in that paragraph has anything to do with military activity?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Well, not particularly, because many of those who went to those detention camps were there as a result of military activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it also fair to say that what appears to be going on based on the language of that paragraph is that at a war presidency meeting, some representative of the Red Cross was apparently present, asked for information about what they were finding in the camps, refused to give it, and received some kind of warning? In other words, it appears that the autonomous region war presidency was trying to get information from the Red Cross about what was going on in the camps. So if necessary, they might be able to take some action regarding it. And the Red Cross refused to give them any information. Isn't that what that says?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I don't think it says that in entirety. It says that -- as it says in the document, that there were complaints about the work of the ICRC, and because they kept their methods and information about conditions to themselves, and they were warned. It doesn't necessarily say that, as you've put in the question, that the ARK Crisis Staff were trying to find out about necessarily all the conditions. I do know that contextually around this time, there were complaints certainly in the military documentation about the work of the ICRC who they viewed not as being impartial, and that they were not portraying accurately the condition in other camps, and that the International Red Cross was coming on ulterior motives of intelligence gathering and the likes. So it's not clear from this necessarily what they were complaining about. But they could have been complaining, for example, about the fact that they viewed the ICRC as not being impartial and were being disingenuous and spreading rumours that conditions in the camps were very bad, but it's not exactly clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Doesn't all this also show up in what is essentially a military document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, it's a military document. It's a military secret confidential coded deliver immediately document. 18 July 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So if it is, what's the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think I've outlined the problem as clearly as I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Move ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're not going to go to the one that you wanted to talk about regarding the ARK Crisis Staff and camps. At the bottom of that paragraph, you talk about "on 23 August during the visit to Manjaca camp by Tadeusz Mazowiecki, UN Special Rapporteur on Human Rights in the former Yugoslavia, members of the ARK Crisis Staff accompanied the visit." That's what you told the Chamber. Right?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What members of the ARK Crisis Staff accompanied Mr. Mazowiecki's visit on the 23rd of August?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: May I have a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let me find it for you. It would be DB286.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's P1777, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe if I take you to the last paragraph, it says: "Regardless of the consequences of the cancellation of Mr. Mazowiecki's visit to the prisoner of war camp, we declare with full responsibility that the purpose of his visit was inspecting of the state of human rights, but on the contrary, intelligence, reconnaissance, which can be confirmed by those representatives of the government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina who were present and who spoke to him."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that doesn't say ARK Crisis Staff members, does it?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: No, but Mr. Radic was present, and I believe he was a member of the ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you think he was present as a member of the ARK Crisis Staff rather than as mayor of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I don't know in what capacity he attended the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why did you tell the Chamber he attended in capacity of ARK Crisis Staff if you don't know?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I didn't say he was attending as part of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just told me that. You just said that. Just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We're getting way off field. He started on cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him finish. It's important. Because it's reading documents and referring to documents, needs to be hundred per cent correct if we are to give weight, hundred per cent weight, to the reports that we receive. I mean, it's being put to the witness that his conclusion that members of the ARK Crisis Staff accompanied the visit does not follow or does not flow from the document to which the expert refers. Namely, this document 270 that we have just been reading. It says not a member of the ARK Crisis Staff, it says "members of the Crisis Staff accompanied the visit." So the question is perfectly legitimate. Did Mr. Brown have a basis on which to conclude that members of the ARK Crisis Staff accompanied the visit, having referred to that document, or didn't he? And if he did, is it a mistake or is it because he has other information which perhaps justified his conclusion but which we don't have a reference to in this particular paragraph of the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour, that those are within the limitation of the questions. I believe it's the way he's trying to characterise the question in the footnote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but Mr. Nicholls, we are not members of a panel of jurors here, we are three professional Judges and we are perfectly capable of taking stock of what is happening. So we are not going to be impressed by Mr. Ackerman becoming suddenly aggressive or raising his voice or whatever. I mean, it doesn't -- these things... I have been doing this work for the past 27 years. So take it from me, nothing impresses me. Yes, Mr. Brown.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot remember if there was other material which I didn't footnote that may have indicated who else was on this visit. That aside, I should have stated in that sentence "a member of the ARK Crisis Staff visited" or "a member" and, to quote the document "representatives of the government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina were present during this visit."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that may have been true if there was an ARK Crisis Staff on 23 August 1992, but there wasn't, was there?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I don't know if there was a Crisis Staff or war presidency during that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't you think before you made that representation to the Trial Chamber you should have found out?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Mr. Radic had been a member of the ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know, but the quotation is that on the 23rd of August 1992, what was the ARK Crisis Staff had already come to an end and there was no longer an ARK Crisis Staff. There is a question, an argument of whether for a part of August it still existed. Formally or informally, I don't know. That is a submission that has been made and which still remains to be seen. But for all intents and purposes it has been put to you that you should have been aware that the ARK Crisis Staff had come to an end, end of July beginning of August, and that therefore on the 23rd of July-- of August you couldn't have safely stated that there were members of the ARK Crisis Staff accompanying Mr. Mazowiecki on this visit. And all the more so, since the document 270, Exhibit DB270, actually never refers to any members of the ARK Crisis Staff, but just members of the government of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I concede, Your Honour, that I maybe should have been more careful in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next question, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, again back to your original language, "on 23 August during the visit to Manjaca camp by Tadeusz Mazowiecki..." Now the impression I think anyone would get from that is Tadeusz Mazowiecki visited Manjaca camp on 23 August. And in fact, that visit never occurred, did it?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: The attempted visit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well you didn't say attempted visit. You left the impression that he went there with members of the ARK Crisis Staff, and he didn't even go there, did he?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: He wasn't allowed in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you leave that out? You knew it, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't you think that shows a pretty high degree of irresponsibility on your part to misinform the Chamber that way?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I had no intention of misinforming anybody, Mr. Ackerman, and this is a large report, and I can only say I should have been more careful in that section. Not much else I can say on that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that may apply to several other sections of your report, also correct? You should have been more careful?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Maybe if you point those out, we can discuss them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If it weren't for cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On the other hand -- one moment, Mr. Ackerman, because we also have to be... If you look at footnote 187, it reads as follows: 1st Krajina Corps report dated 23rd of August. And please note the date. On the visit Manjaca camp by Tadeusz Mazowiecki which was denied. So there is a statement to the effect based on the Krajina report, on the 1st Krajina Corps report, that the visit to Manjaca was actually denied. But in any case, I mean, the point is made by both of you, both by you, Mr. Ackerman, and Mr. Brown. And I fully degree if you read the last part of the last sentence of the paragraph 1.113 for the record, it is in itself misleading in a sense that it tends to suggest that there was a visit on the 23rd of August by Tadeusz Mazowiecki at which he was accompanied by members of the ARK Crisis Staff. And as such, this is not correct. I'm not imputing at all that this was intentionally inserted in the report to mislead the Trial Chamber. We're not taking it as that also because of the footnote that I referred to. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let's go to paragraph 1.114.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tell the Chamber there that "ARK Crisis Staff members - plural - also toured the areas of combat activity and were briefed by military personnel in order to gain an understanding of the situation." And then the only reference that you give the Chamber with regard to that contention, that members toured the areas, is one visit by Mr. Brdjanin to Kotor Varos and another by Brdjanin to Operation Corridor in 1992. What other members of the ARK Crisis Staff toured areas of combat activity that you can tell the Chamber about?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: There's a reference in the previous paragraph about delegation going to Prijedor and the Kozarski Vjesnik article characterised that as areas of combat operations had taken place and collection centres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: And I believe Kozarski Vjesnik article makes reference to Mr. Radic and Mr. Brdjanin and others. There's the Vojo Kupresanin visit to Manjaca camp. So there are one or two articles there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Chamber should treat that phrase "ARK Crisis Staff members also toured areas of combat activity and were briefed by military personnel in order to gain a better understanding of the situation" to mean areas of previous combat activity or previous combat activity or places where there had never been any combat activity? I mean, that's the way it should be read according to you now.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I can just give you the three or four examples that I've just cited, that certain members did tour the area. And Mr. Brdjanin's own words in the video, that the idea was to gain an understanding of the situation on the ground. He makes mention that he had been into the corridor, and he's clearly in Kotor Varos at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Ackerman is fully justified in drawing your attention to this because the paragraph starts with "ARK Crisis Staff members," but then the reference is only to two instances, both of which seemingly at least on the face of it, because I don't have the documents here in front of me, refer to Radoslav Brdjanin, to Radoslav Brdjanin only. It may well be that there were other instances which you may have had in your mind and which you rightly referred to in drawing your own conclusions. But the point is that they are not indicated here as footnotes. So this is the problem. And the other problem is that again, you state that ARK Crisis Staff members also toured the areas of combat activity and were briefed by military personnel in order to gain an understanding of the situation. Were they briefed by military personnel in order to gain an understanding of the situation when they toured the areas of combat activity, or were the two activities separate? In other words, one could have taken place independently of the other. Because it could well be for example that reports were made regularly or irregularly during meetings of the ARK Crisis Staff by members of the armed forces, by members of the 1st Krajina Corps. I don't know. I mean, it's -- what did you base your conclusions upon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have used the other references in the previous paragraph, so the reference to the visit to Prijedor I used in the previous paragraph, the Kozarski Vjesnik article, which does reference. Radic and Brdjanin and others I believe being briefed by Mr. Adzic and others. I could have refootnoted it and included it there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but we need to keep distinct and apart the ARK Crisis Staff members and the representatives of the ARK government and Banja Luka Municipality because that's the reference you make when you're mentioning the visit to Prijedor. The visit to Prijedor took place -- "by the representatives of the ARK government and Banja Luka Municipality." When you refer to Vojo Kupresanin as visiting Manjaca, which I do not equate with a visit to an area of combat activity, you refer to him as president of ARK assembly and also ARK Crisis Staff member. So it's this confusion of, you know, representatives from here, representatives from there all being put seemingly in the same basket to make a point. And the point simply gets confused because -- do we have proof of ARK Crisis Staff members touring the areas of combat activity apart from Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the capacity of the ARK Crisis Staff are you asking?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, because then you state "ARK Crisis Staff members," and then you refer only to Radoslav Brdjanin. There were other members. I've lost count of how many members there were. But are you aware of any other ARK Crisis Staff member touring the areas of combat activity, and then also any other ARK Crisis Staff member apart from Radoslav Brdjanin who was briefed by military personnel in order, et cetera? Either during one of these visits or before or after or having nothing to do with any of these visits?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only reference the Prijedor one where they are referenced as being briefed by Colonel Arsic and military commanders in Prijedor. I believe that document reference makes mention that they were -- I would have to reread the document actually because I don't remember what -- if they say "ARK Crisis Staff members were briefed" or members of the regional government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Maybe at the time you drafted these paragraphs, that was not important. But you realise now how important it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do. And I can only go back to my answer, that this document, I was not set the task by the legal staff here to finesse and nuance every ARK Crisis Staff or government decision in relation to who briefed what. And I put this -- these paragraphs, and I again I apologise if they are unclear. I put these paragraphs in the wider section relating to civilian cooperation to articulate that civilian cooperation was a feature in operations or the activities in 1992. That's what I put in. I wasn't asked to put it in to finesse and nuance and explain every relationship between the members of the ARK Crisis Staff. I wasn't given that task. I wanted to get over in these paragraphs, unclear as they may be, that civilian cooperation was a feature, and an important feature. And there is some evidence that it was a feature in this regional-level government, both from the military perspective, and some limited documentation that I have seen, I may not have seen it all, from the governments at the various assembly or the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But for the accused, that is very important because the accused was president of or it being alleged that he was president of the ARK Crisis Staff. And it is being alleged that the ARK Crisis Staff itself had no teeth, and not even a legal basis for its authority, if authority it had. That's what is being submitted. So actually, if there was delegation that went to Prijedor which Mr. Radic, for example, formed part or even headed, I don't know, then it's being alleged that you cannot, unless you have the appropriate basis for it, appropriate documents to rely upon, you cannot in your report tell us that Mr. Radic went there as a member of the ARK Crisis Staff because that, for the Defence, is very important. If he went there as a member of the ARK Crisis Staff, obviously it has its importance. If Mr. Brdjanin went there as president of the ARK Crisis Staff, of course that has its importance. But if you're saying that there were other members of the ARK Crisis Staff that visited these combat zones, areas of combat activity as you put it, when in actual fact there was no evidence to show that, the suggestion by the Defence is, dear Judges, please ignore his expert report because it is based on assumptions and not on facts. This is what is being put to you and to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Your Honour, and I can only articulate that that type of argument was not necessarily -- was not the agreement on the basis my report was written on. And what I wanted to do in this section was to look at the issue of civil/military cooperation and try and portray the fact that from the documents I have seen, and limited they may have been, that civilian/military cooperation existed. It existed at municipal level, there's evidence that there was this regional level cooperation as well, and finally, another example from Western Slavonia that the JNA and VRS at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Ackerman, you've made your second point. I invite you to move to the next question, if you have finished with this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, I just want to say in connection with this issue which we have been talking about, on the direct examination, in fairness to the accused, we went through the transcript where he said that he toured all the areas of combat activity in the corridor in his capacity as president of the ARK Crisis Staff. So that main point has made clearly, and as well as in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but the whole thing is the suggestion that this is not an accurate report, and even if it may say so in so many words with regard to some aspects, you should look at it with circumspection, keeping in mind these points that are being referred to, it is not only precise but it is based on assumptions and not on facts. This is the suggestion. I don't think that Mr. Ackerman is as such contesting that there is a footage in which Radoslav Brdjanin himself supposedly states that he was - I don't know where - or that there is an official notebook that mentions Brdjanin as visiting, et cetera. He may contest that this visit ever took place. But that's not the point. The point is that in paragraph 1.114 supposes or suggests that -- not just Radoslav Brdjanin, but ARK Crisis Staff members. And there is a reference to documents, and that statement is not borne out by those references. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated when you were responding Judge Agius that all you were trying to accomplish here was to show military/civil cooperation between the military and civilian authorities. So I take it from that that you have no indication from what you're telling us here, and you do not contend, that any of this documentation shows Crisis Staff control, ARK Crisis Staff control, over military units, does it?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I do not see the ARK Crisis Staff necessarily controlling military units per se in a strict subordination manner. I do see in some areas, for example, the issue of weapon deadlines, decisions taken at the ARK Crisis Staff which clearly led to some military activity on the ground which were involved in attacks on municipalities in the Krajina area. And there are other areas such as, say, the removal of Muslims from the military which clearly a decision at the ARK Crisis Staff led to activity in the military. But as to the ARK Crisis Staff controlling military units in a subordinated way, I do not see that. And in that respect, you're right, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer just opened about 30 minutes of questions which I will have to do tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Brown. I thank you, Mr. Ackerman, Mr. Nicholls. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00. In which courtroom, Madam Registrar? Is it this one again? I think it's the whole week. No? If it is possible to shift to another courtroom, please, let's try and do that. I don't know if it is at all possible. Yes, your client has discovered a horrendous mistake somewhere in the transcript, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We'll find it and take care of it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of October, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.
